column3: LF-by-default text policy: `* text=auto eol=lf`, CRLF forced for *.bat/*.cmd/*.ps1, `-whitespace` on archived packages/agent/docs/**/*.diff so patch artifacts keep whitespace exactly, and binary markers for png/jpg/gif/webp/ico/pdf/zip/gz/woff.

Repo hygiene list: node_modules, dist/, .artifacts/, packages/ai/src/providers/data/ (hydrated model data is never staged), packages/ai/src/providers/.model-generation-*/, local user state (.pi/settings.json, .pi/hf-sessions/), and scratch names (todo.md, plans/, collect.sh, out.jsonl).

Pre-commit gate: scripts/check-lockfile-commit.mjs first (blocks accidental lockfile commits), then `npm run check` (biome + tsc + 5 static checks), a staged-file-scoped browser-smoke run that only fires when packages/ai/ or package.json changed, and re-staging of files the formatter rewrote.
Two-line supply-chain policy: save-exact=true pins every direct dependency to an exact version; min-release-age=2 makes npm refuse any release published less than two days ago.

Operating rules for humans and agents: read files in full before wide-ranging changes, no dynamic/inline imports, erasable-only TypeScript (Node strip-only mode), never hand-edit packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts, never run the full vitest suite (it activates live-API e2e) but ./test.sh instead, and git rules that protect concurrent agent sessions (stage explicit paths, never git add -A / reset --hard / stash).

Biome 2.3.5 lint+format config: tab indent width 3, line width 120, recommended rules with noExplicitAny/noNonNullAssertion/noEmptyInterface off, an explicit include list (packages/*/src, packages/*/test, examples) that excludes generated models.generated.ts and *.models.ts, plus a custom Grit plugin (scripts/biome/model-type-comparison.grit).

Contribution policy: "pi's core is minimal" — anything that does not belong in the core should be an extension; "you must understand your code"; new-contributor issues and PRs are auto-closed until a maintainer replies `lgtm`; `npm run check` and `./test.sh` must both pass; do not edit CHANGELOG.md (maintainers do).
Generated Nix lockfile (version 7) pinning two nixpkgs inputs by rev + narHash: nixos-unstable and a separate nixpkgs-26.05-darwin input.

Nix flake exposing packages + apps for aarch64/x86_64 on linux/darwin, with a second nixpkgs input pinned to the last Darwin branch that still supports Intel macOS, and an overlay that re-exports the package.
Standard MIT license text, Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner — pure boilerplate, no mechanism.
Three-line pin of the model catalog by CONTENT hash (a sha256 revision). This single string is the offline build's catalog source of truth and the input the Nix build fetches.

Nix packaging: builds the workspace packages from source, hydrates the pinned catalog offline, packs each package to a tarball, installs the separate install-lock tree with internal packages overridden by the locally built tarballs, wraps the CLI with fd/ripgrep/clipboard on PATH, and runs an installCheck that asserts `pi --version` and `require()`s the TUI native prebuilds so a missing native dep fails the build instead of silently disabling clipboard support.

Generated npm lockfile (lockfileVersion 3, 6451 lines of resolved registry URLs + integrity hashes). I opened the head (root package block plus the first dependency entries) to confirm it is the monorepo root lockfile for package.json; not read line by line because it is mechanical dependency metadata with no harness mechanism.

Root workspace manifest: the packages/* workspaces plus five example-extension workspaces, the build/check/version/release script set, `check` as a chain of biome + pinned-dep + runtime-dep + ts-import + entry-graph + install-lock gates then `tsc --noEmit` then browser smoke, exact-pinned devDependencies (biome 2.3.5, typescript 7.0.2, esbuild 0.28.2), and a protobufjs 7.6.6 override.

One-line type re-export shim (`export * from "./dist/bedrock-provider.js"`); exists so the published subpath resolves from a source checkout where dist/ is not built yet — the built artifact comes from src/bedrock-provider.ts.
One-line runtime re-export shim pointing at the same built artifact as the sibling .d.ts.

Changelog of the ai package: read lines 1-260 and grepped the whole file for retry / context-overflow / classifier / compat mechanisms. It is the historical record of provider-abstraction decisions (per-model compat flags, mid-conversation tool changes, cache-affinity header formats, cross-provider thinking-block dropping). Older release bodies not read line by line.

Published manifest for @earendil-works/pi-ai 1.4.0: wildcard ./api/*, ./utils/*, ./providers/* export subpaths (the code-splitting surface), an explicit sideEffects list so the compat/image registries are not tree-shaken away, a `pi-ai` bin for `login`/`list`, and build scripts that regenerate models, typecheck, then copy hydrated provider data into dist.

The ai package's public API contract, read in full (1995 lines): provider/model abstraction (Provider owns catalog+auth+stream; Models routes), auth resolution order, credential store contract, streaming event reference, tool definition/validation, the ~50 `compat` flags, system-message sections, faux provider for tests, and cross-provider handoff rules.
Build config for the ai package: NodeNext module + resolution, outDir dist, rootDir src, and exclusion of every .d.ts (hand-written declarations under src are not re-emitted).

Vitest config for the ai package: node environment, 30s timeout "for API calls", dot reporter (github-actions reporter when GITHUB_ACTIONS is set), silent:"passed-only", and an alias pointing @earendil-works/pi-telemetry at the telemetry SOURCE rather than dist.
One line: ignores *.bun-build artifacts from the Bun single-file binary build.

Changelog of the coding-agent package (6367 lines): read lines 1-820 and grepped the whole file for compaction / steering / system-prompt / retry / extension-boundary mechanisms. It is where pi's design decisions are recorded with their reasons. Older release bodies (lines 820-6367) not read line by line.

Generated npm lockfile for the installer-only lock root (1507 lines of resolved registry URLs + integrity hashes). I opened the head to confirm it pins @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.4.0 plus its full transitive tree; not read line by line because it is mechanical dependency metadata.

Installer lock root: a private package whose ONLY dependency is @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent at an exact version, so the pi.dev installer gets a pinned transitive tree while the plain npm install deliberately does not.

Published manifest for @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.4.0: `piConfig.configDir: ".pi"` declares the config directory from inside the package, the files list ships docs/examples/schemas, build:binary compiles a Bun single-file binary, copy-assets copies themes/assets/html-export templates into dist, and the schema/reference generators run through the TS source-resolver.
Package-level install and dev README: `npm install --ignore-scripts`, `./pi-test.sh` (callable from any directory), and the required `npm run check` + `./test.sh` before submitting a PR.

Generated JSON Schema for keybindings.json: every binding is a dotted action id (tui.editor.*, app.session.*, app.tree.filter.*, app.message.followUp/dequeue) with a one-line human description, a regex-constrained KeybindingValue (string or string[] of modifier+key, negative lookahead forbidding a doubled modifier), and additionalProperties allowed so custom bindings still validate.

Generated JSON Schema for models.json — the provider/model abstraction as pure data: providers[] with baseUrl/api/apiKey ("$NAME" env interpolation or "!command")/headers/compat, models[] with per-model api/baseUrl/thinkingLevelMap/inputLimits/cost/promptCache/contextWindow/samplingParams, a modelOverrides map, and a ~600-line ProviderCompat block of capability flags (supportsMidConvoSystemMessages, supportsMidConvoToolAdditions, supportsStrictTools, allowedFallbackModels, thinkingFormat, cacheControlFormat, sessionAffinityFormat…).

Generated JSON Schema for settings.json — the whole runtime config surface: steeringMode and followUpMode (both default "one-at-a-time"), compaction.reserveTokens (16384) + keepRecentTokens (20000) + per-model modelOverrides, retry (maxRetries 3, baseDelayMs 2000, maxAgentDelayMs 60000, provider.maxRetryDelayMs "Maximum server-requested delay before failing"), codemode.mode, cacheWarming (off|streaming|idle, global only), doubleEscapeAction, treeFilterMode, and deprecated legacy keys kept for migration.

Generated JSON Schema for theme.json: a required color set (~50 named colors covering tool boxes, diff, markdown and thinking-level borders) with documented fallbacks for optional keys (scrollbarTrack→muted, thinkingMax→thinkingXhigh, searchMatchBg→selectedBg), a ColorValue that is hex/OKLCH/OKHSL/variable/empty-string OR a 0-255 palette index, and additionalProperties:false so a typo'd color is rejected.

Generates the human-readable models-configuration.md reference FROM the same TypeBox schemas the validator uses: it derives a type string per field, only recurses into nested objects that carry a description or default, and links top-level fields to other sections instead of expanding them — so the docs and the validator cannot drift apart.

Generates the four published JSON Schemas from TypeBox: splits JSON-Schema annotation keys from shape keys, dedups repeated sub-schemas into $defs by JSON shape identity while preserving per-use annotations, and THROWS "Unused schema definitions" when a declared definition is never referenced, so a dead $defs entry fails the build.

One-shot migration for sessions written to the wrong directory by a v0.30.0 bug: reads each JSONL's first line with jq, encodes the cwd into the sessions/<encoded-cwd>/ name, skips on any parse failure or existing target (never overwrites), and supports --dry-run.
Build config for the coding agent: `paths` resolve @earendil-works/pi-agent-core/pi-ai/pi-tui to the built .d.ts of sibling packages, and src/experimental is excluded from the published build.
Separate noEmit config for examples/, resolving workspace packages to SOURCE rather than dist so an example can exercise an API that is not published yet.

Vitest config for the coding agent: env PI_OFFLINE=1 by default with an explicit allowNetwork() opt-in, unstubEnvs, 30s timeout, photon-node externalized, and aliases resolving pi-ai/pi-agent-core/pi-tui (plus the legacy @mariozechner/* names) to workspace source.
Windows launcher: delegates to pi-test.ps1 through powershell.exe with -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, and fails with a clear "powershell.exe not found" message instead of a cryptic error.
Runs pi from TypeScript sources via `node --import <source-resolver file URL> cli.ts`; the --no-env flag unsets 36 provider/API/cloud credential env vars before launching.

POSIX twin of pi-test.ps1: unsets the same credential list under --no-env, and converts the source-resolver path to a file:// URL because --import takes a module specifier (raw paths break on #, ?, %).

Top-level product README: the package table (chord, telemetry, pi-ai, durable, pi-agent-core, pi-coding-agent, pi-tui), the explicit "Pi does not include a built-in permission system" statement with three named containerization patterns, and the supply-chain-hardening section (exact pins, min-release-age, install-lock, npm audit signatures).

Explicit trust-boundary statement: pi runs with the user's own permissions, files writable by that account are inside the trust boundary, prompt injection and malicious trusted extensions/skills are explicitly OUT of scope, and reports that require prior local write access are not vulnerabilities.

The test harness: mktemp an isolated HOME/TMPDIR/npm-config tree, then run `npm test` under `env -i` with an explicit allowlist (PATH, HOME, XDG_*, GIT_*, CI) so ambient credentials cannot reach a paid API; the cleanup trap refuses to delete anything that is not the marked, non-symlink directory it created.

Shared compiler options: target/lib ES2024, strict, erasableSyntaxOnly (Node strip-only mode — no enum/namespace/parameter properties), verbatimModuleSyntax, allowImportingTsExtensions + rewriteRelativeImportExtensions, declaration maps and inline sources.

Root typecheck config: noEmit, NodeNext, a path map covering every workspace package and subpath (chord/context/delta/node/output/sqlite, telemetry, codemode, mcp, ai, durable, env, agent, coding-agent, tui), and an include list spanning packages/*/src, packages/*/test, the durable test workers, and both examples trees.

Shared vitest base: a table of workspace source paths plus a resolve.alias list mapping every workspace package (and pi-ai's api/*, utils/*, providers/* wildcards) to SOURCE files, so each package's tests run against source rather than a stale built dist.
